title: Long QCOM — Dragonfly Inference Layer Debut; Meta as Anchor Data Center Customer
entry: Long $190-205 (buy the pullback from +12% gap-open on Dragonfly launch). QCOM gapped to $202-203 premarket on June 25 on the Dragonfly C1000 CPU + Meta anchor customer announcement, then faded intraday to $191-197 as the market sold the gap. Entry in the $190-205 range is buying the digestion phase post-announcement, not chasing the gap. Scale: 60% on June 25 session in the $191-197 pullback range; 40% add on any second-day weakness to $190-193. Do NOT enter above $210 — at that level the announcement is fully priced for the near term and the risk/reward compresses to sub-1:2.
stop_loss: $180 daily close (~9% below $198 midpoint) — implies the Dragonfly launch is a product announcement without commercial traction, OR Meta cancels or delays the C1000 data center deployment (Zuckerberg walks back the capital commitment at a future event), OR QCOM Q3 FY2026 earnings guidance (expected late July) disappoints on data center ramp timeline
targets: $215 — first confirmation: sell-side begins C1000 data center revenue model buildout; Barclays, UBS initiate QCOM AI infrastructure models; +8.7% from $198 midpoint

$230 — second customer announced: Apple, Amazon, or Google validates QCOM Dragonfly for edge/private cloud deployment alongside Meta; QCOM P/E re-rates toward Marvell/Broadcom AI infrastructure comps at 24-26x; +16.2%
$250 — QCOM Q3 FY2026 earnings (late July) includes first Dragonfly revenue recognition or backlog disclosure; sell-side consensus moves to >$12 EPS for FY2027 on data center contribution; +26.3%
catalyst: QCOM unveiled the Dragonfly C1000 data center inference CPU on June 25, 2026, with Meta Platforms as the first anchor customer — confirmed by Mark Zuckerberg's announcement that Meta is deploying Dragonfly across its inference workloads. QCOM gapped +12% premarket on the news (from $204 prior close to ~$228 peak premarket), then faded to $191-203 intraday as the initial gap drew profit-taking. The Dragonfly positions QCOM alongside Marvell and Broadcom in the custom silicon / data center inference layer that has been the highest-multiple segment of the AI infrastructure buildout. Meta's anchor customer status validates commercial readiness immediately — this is not vaporware with a future ship date but a product with a named enterprise buyer at scale.
thesis:
QCOM has been the largest missing piece in the AI semiconductor infrastructure build-out. Its Snapdragon mobile dominance is mature and slower-growth; its automotive/IoT revenue streams are real but not valued at AI multiples. The Dragonfly C1000 changes the valuation framework: if QCOM can establish a 10-15% data center CPU share in the AI inference layer (a market projected to grow from $8B in 2026 to $35B+ by 2029), the incremental EPS contribution justifies a P/E re-rating from the current ~18x to 24-26x — the multiple Broadcom ($AVGO) carries for its custom AI silicon business. Meta is not just a revenue source; it is a reference customer that de-risks sales cycles with hyperscalers. Every subsequent hyperscaler evaluating inference infrastructure will benchmark against Dragonfly's Meta deployment, compressing the QCOM enterprise sales cycle from 18-24 months to 6-9 months for the next tier.

The technical setup is favorable for entry. QCOM gapped from $204 to ~$228 premarket (+12%) but immediately sold off as momentum traders took the news-day profit. The $191-203 intraday range represents the digestion zone — the stock finding its new fundamental clearing price post-announcement, not a reversal of the thesis. Historical AI catalyst gaps (NVDA post-earnings, AMD post-CDNA announcements) show that day-one gap digestion typically stabilizes 8-12% below the gap high before the fundamental re-rating cycle restarts as sell-side models catch up. That implies $195-205 is the digestion floor, consistent with the entry range.

The risk is execution: QCOM's Dragonfly C1000 needs to demonstrate competitive inference throughput vs. NVIDIA H100/H200 and AMD MI300X in real workloads. If Meta's deployment reveals performance gaps — latency, memory bandwidth, or software ecosystem limitations — the story collapses before the second customer announcement. QCOM also faces the CUDA moat: Meta uses PyTorch (which it co-developed and maintains), giving it more flexibility to run non-CUDA inference than most hyperscalers, but the broader industry is still CUDA-native. The $180 stop is firm — if QCOM trades back through its pre-announcement price, the market is telling you the Dragonfly launch failed to land commercially.
bull_case: Meta deploys 50,000+ C1000 units in Q3 2026 (disclosed in Q2 earnings call late July); Amazon announces a competing order for AWS Graviton-style QCOM inference chips within 4 weeks. QCOM guided to $3B+ in Dragonfly revenue for H2 FY2026 at Q3 earnings (late July), driving consensus EPS upgrades of 20-25%. Stock re-rates from $197 to $250+ (Target 3) over 6 weeks as sell-side updates AI infrastructure models to include QCOM as the third leg alongside NVDA and AMD.
bear_case: Dragonfly benchmarks released by independent researchers show C1000 inference throughput 30-40% behind NVIDIA H100 at equivalent power consumption. Meta's deployment remains limited to non-latency-sensitive workloads (batch inference, recommendation re-ranking) rather than real-time generative AI. Sell-side maintains QCOM at mobile/automotive multiples. Stock fades from $197 back toward $185-190 as the gap is fully filled. Stop at $180 triggered if the thesis deteriorates further.
invalidation: $180 daily close; OR Meta publicly discloses that Dragonfly deployment is paused or limited to a pilot (sub-1,000 units); OR QCOM Q3 FY2026 earnings guidance (late July) excludes material Dragonfly revenue contribution; OR NVIDIA announces a competing edge/inference chip that directly targets the C1000 use case, causing QCOM to lose the benchmark comparison narrative
